items.followUp: Explain how temperature affects the rate of evaporation.

rubric.why: Identifies that strong intermolecular forces slow evaporation.
rubric.description: Strong intermolecular forces make evaporation slower.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking strong intermolecular forces with slower evaporation.

rubric.why: Identifies that weak intermolecular forces allow molecules to escape more easily.
rubric.description: Weak intermolecular forces make evaporation faster.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking weak intermolecular forces with faster evaporation.

modelAnswer: When intermolecular forces are strong, more energy is needed for molecules to escape from the liquid, so evaporation is slower.
When intermolecular forces are weak, molecules escape more easily, so evaporation is faster.

items.followUp: Why is aluminium also used for making electrical wires?

rubric.why: Identifies copper's ability to conduct electricity.
rubric.description: Copper is an excellent conductor of electricity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that copper conducts electricity well.

rubric.why: Identifies the property that lets copper be shaped into wires.
rubric.description: Copper is ductile and can be drawn into thin wires.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that copper is ductile or can be drawn into wires.

modelAnswer: Copper is an excellent conductor of electricity.
It is ductile, so it can be drawn into thin wires.

items.followUp: Why does oxygen usually have a valency of two?

rubric.why: Identifies the number of electrons in chlorine's outermost shell.
rubric.description: Chlorine has seven electrons in its outermost shell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chlorine has seven valence electrons.

rubric.why: Explains that chlorine needs one electron to complete its outer shell and therefore has valency one.
rubric.description: Chlorine needs one more electron to complete its outer shell; its valency is one.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the one-electron requirement and the resulting valency of one.

modelAnswer: A chlorine atom has seven electrons in its outermost shell.
It needs one more electron to complete that shell; therefore, its valency is one.

items.followUp: Write the chemical formula for aluminium oxide using the valencies of aluminium and oxygen.

rubric.why: Begins the formula-writing method with the symbols of the elements or ions.
rubric.description: Write the symbols of the elements or ions, such as Mg and Cl.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the correct symbols for the example.

rubric.why: Identifies the valencies needed to determine the formula subscripts.
rubric.description: Write the valencies: Mg = 2 and Cl = 1.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating the valencies in the example.

rubric.why: Applies the interchange method and simplifies the subscripts to obtain the correct formula.
rubric.description: Interchange the valencies as subscripts, then remove the subscript 1 to obtain MgCl₂.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for correctly interchanging the valencies and simplifying to the formula MgCl₂.

rubric.why: Includes the bracket rule for repeated polyatomic ions.
rubric.description: Put a polyatomic ion in brackets when it occurs more than once, before writing its subscript.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the correct bracket rule.

modelAnswer: Write the symbols of the elements or ions; for example, Mg and Cl.
Write their valencies: Mg = 2 and Cl = 1.
Interchange the valencies and write them as subscripts: Mg₁Cl₂.
Remove the subscript 1 to obtain MgCl₂.
If a polyatomic ion occurs more than once, put it in brackets before writing its subscript.
